knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.2.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes a confidence interval for an unknown parameter based on a random sample?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the parameter-CI reading (not a prediction claim).
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: A parameter CI targets an unknown parameter with frequentist coverage. Covering a future observation is a prediction interval. A naive post-data probability-on-the-parameter reading is not the frequentist coverage claim.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Interval for an unknown parameter from sample evidence, with stated frequentist coverage.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Reading a parameter CI as a prediction interval or as a post-data probability on the parameter.

choices.label: A confidence interval uses random-sample evidence to give an interval for an unknown parameter, with a stated frequentist coverage interpretation under repeated sampling.
A confidence interval is an interval that contains the next future observation with the stated probability.
After the data are observed, a 95% confidence interval means there is a 95% probability that the fixed unknown parameter lies in that specific numerical interval, in the Bayesian posterior sense.
A confidence interval is simply any interval estimate of a future loss, whether or not a parameter is targeted.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.2.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. From a large sample you obtain a 95% CI for mean claim size μ as (120, 140). Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Interpret the parameter CI; refuse prediction reading.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Frequentist coverage is about the procedure and the parameter μ, not about the next observation. Treating μ as a random draw inside the interval, or equating narrowness with certainty, misstates coverage.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: 95% coverage for μ under repeated sampling; not a prediction interval for the next claim.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Reading the CI as a 95% probability for the next observation.

choices.label: The interval comes from a procedure that covers the unknown parameter μ in 95% of repeated samples. It is not a claim that the next claim amount falls between 120 and 140 with probability 95%.
There is a 95% probability that the next claim amount falls between 120 and 140.
μ is a random variable that equals 130 with probability 95%, and the interval endpoints are fixed constants only.
Because the interval is narrow, coverage must be exactly 100% for this particular sample.
